lead_headline: Lost Coffee debuts sixth Colorado location in Arvada as Moore. Cafe preps second gluten-free bakery in Lakewood — 4 new leads today

restaurant.blurb: 4 new leads today: Lost Coffee (Arvada, sixth Colorado location), Moore. Cafe (Lakewood gluten-free bakery), Tacos el Comando (Aurora closure), Pelican Bay (Cherry Creek marina shuttered).

liquor.blurb: Zero applications for the seventh consecutive day — the post-flood silence now extends to ten total days since the April 29-30 deluge dumped 2,144 renewals. The 7-day window flatlines at 0 versus last week's 2,386-application surge, a complete evaporation from the typical 20-30 weekly baseline. No official word from state licensing on when the pipeline reopens or whether backend cleanup continues. The freeze deepens into its second full week with zero queue visibility — applications either held offline awaiting batch release or caught in post-flood reconciliation. May's licensing picture remains entirely dark as Saturday marks day ten of the blackout.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention yesterday (Cherry Hills mansion sale) drops Friday to the week's quietest day, but the 7-day total holds at 49 across 7 sources — up 14% from last week's 43. Denver Post dominates with 17 mentions (35% share), trailed by Instagram (13), X and Facebook (5 each), with real estate and golf aggregator coverage anchoring the week. The 49-mention total runs 14% above last week and matches the 30-day rolling average — outlets sustain baseline engagement heading into the weekend despite Friday's single-mention lull. Social platforms drive discovery (48 via Google News RSS, 1 via Reddit), while traditional media pickups remain consistent. Week-over-week growth persists as the editorial cycle normalizes after midweek bankruptcy coverage.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −2 yesterday (0 new, 2 canceled) pulls MTD to +15 (+1.7/day) while 90-day net holds at +134. Two Friday cancellations follow Thursday's zero-churn day, marking the second consecutive loss after an eight-day clean streak. This week still posts +10 net (15 new, 5 canceled), reversing last week's −1 (19 new, 20 canceled) as acquisition tightens but churn creeps higher. MTD's +1.7/day rate runs 31% ahead of YTD's +1.3/day baseline despite the weekend slide — the pattern shows retention loosening slightly from mid-week's zero-cancel performance, but May's momentum absorbs the Friday bleed without major damage. Acquisition volumes remain compressed (15 this week vs 19 last), suggesting slower inbound flow even as retention holds structurally sound.
